extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and taste profile for authors submitting fiction, select YA/middle grade, narrative nonfiction, and memoir to agent Hillary Jacobson; includes the kinds of stories she seeks, examples of comparable titles, diversity preferences, and submission format instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional / cultural impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts that 'provoke a strong emotional reaction, add an important perspective to the cultural conversation or force the reader to challenge what they think.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally a submission will achieve one or more of these outcomes — provoking strong emotion, contributing an important perspective, or challenging readers' assumptions (or all of the above). This is a primary taste marker for what will make a book stand out to the agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protagonist focus: 'complicated women'
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent's brand described as 'complicated women' — she gravitates to stories centered on complex female characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that foregrounds layered, morally ambiguous, or emotionally complex women aligns with the agent's established taste; example favorites listed give a sense of tone and character types she enjoys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target categories sought
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively looking for upmarket, literary, and commercial fiction; select young adult and middle grade; narrative non-fiction and memoir.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a broad-stroke description of the kinds of submissions of interest; authors should map their project to these categories when querying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epic love stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeking sweeping, grand-scale romantic narratives characterized as 'epic love stories.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of tone or comparable novels are provided elsewhere on the page; an epic love story should feel expansive in scope and emotional stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glamorous-world fiction (escapism or social commentary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction that immerses the reader in a glamorous world, either for pure escapism or to deliver biting social commentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should convincingly render a glamorous setting and use it either as an escapist pleasure or as a vehicle for critique; clarity about which approach the manuscript takes will help the agent assess fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Books about books and other art forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested in fiction that centers on books, literary life, or other arts (painting, film, music, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narratives that engage meta-literary themes or are rooted in creative/artistic milieus are welcome; examples of comparable titles are listed on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upmarket romance / rom-com in specific vein
rubrics_metrics.description: Looking for upmarket romance or rom-coms 'in the vein of GHOSTS, THE HUSBANDS, SEVEN DAYS IN JUNE, or EVVIE DRAKE STARTS OVER.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone should balance commercial appeal and literary sensibility (upmarket). Listing specific comparable titles indicates desired voice, pacing, and emotional register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sweeping family saga with compelling hook
rubrics_metrics.description: A sweeping family saga with a compelling, distinctive hook — like BLACK CAKE, HELLO, BEAUTIFUL, REAL AMERICANS, THE LATECOMER, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent favors multigenerational family narratives that open with a strong premise or hook that sustains momentum across the saga.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smart, moving stories with whimsy (food emphasis bonus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that are intelligent and emotionally moving with a touch of whimsy; 'bonus points for the emphasis on the food!'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include LESSONS IN CHEMISTRY and THE STORIED LIFE OF AJ FIKRY; a culinary or food-related element that enriches character and setting is a plus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculative fiction with a twist or touch of magic
rubrics_metrics.description: Speculative fiction that features a world like ours with a twist or a touch of magic (examples: THE IMMORTALISTS, STATION ELEVEN, THE INVISIBLE LIFE OF ADDIE LARUE, NEVER LET ME GO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for grounded speculative worlds — recognizable reality with an intriguing speculative element; comparison titles indicate the kind of emotional/lyrical balance desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspense / 'secrets & lies' — dark, disturbing, unsettling
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspense novels characterized as 'secrets & lies' — agent gravitates toward the dark and disturbing and loves feeling unsettled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include THE PERFECT NANNY and THE QUIET TENANT; good suspense for this agent combines psychological intensity with a persistent sense of unease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character-driven domestic suspense
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspense that allows readers to deeply get to know the characters (in the vein of Liane Moriarty or Sally Hepworth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent enjoys domestic suspense where relational dynamics and well-drawn characters are central, not just plot twists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary suspense (topical or satirical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary suspense that can be serious and topical (e.g., LONG BRIGHT RIVER) or playful and satirical (e.g., SOCIAL CREATURE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open to both feast-for-thought literary takes on suspense and lighter satirical approaches; tone and intent should be clear in the query/first pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open to horror-leaning work
rubrics_metrics.description: Willing to consider submissions that veer into the horror space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Horror submissions should still align with the agent's overall taste for strong character, voice, or literary quality even if they emphasize genre scares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoirs that read like tightly plotted suspenseful fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefers memoirs that 'read like tightly plotted and suspenseful fiction' (examples: BRAIN ON FIRE, WILD GAME, THE FACT OF A BODY).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative nonfiction should have strong structure, narrative drive, and a compelling arc similarly to a suspense novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: YA: 'Gossip Girl meets X' pitchability
rubrics_metrics.description: For YA, she is 'a sucker for anything that can be (accurately) pitched as GOSSIP GIRL meets X,' like ANNA K or THE THOUSANDTH FLOOR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-gloss, socially-driven YA concepts that can be succinctly pitched as a recognizable mash-up are attractive; an accurate comp-pitch helps convey tone and market.

rubrics_metrics.name: YA: High-concept contemporary
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested in high-concept contemporary YA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contemporary YA with a clear, novel hook or premise that can be succinctly described.

rubrics_metrics.name: YA: Grounded fantasy / speculative
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeking grounded fantasy or speculative YA — worlds with imaginative elements but emotional realism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: YA should balance speculative elements with relatable character stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: YA: Historical with a magical twist
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested in historical YA that incorporates a magical twist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical setting should be evocative and the magical element should enhance theme/character rather than overwhelm historical authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: #ownvoices and underrepresented perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: '#ownvoices! I’m committed to promoting underrepresented voices.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong preference for #ownvoices projects and a stated commitment to promoting writers from underrepresented communities; such provenance is a positive factor in consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest in non-US settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent is 'always eager to read stories not set in the US.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions set outside the U.S. are welcome and may be especially interesting; indicate setting clearly in the query.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format: pitch + first ten pages in email body
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should be emailed to hillary.jacobson@caa.com with your pitch and the first ten pages of your manuscript in the body of the email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agent states she responds to every query and average response time is about a month. Note that older ICM email forwards will still reach her; follow the specified format to ensure quick review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to consider outside-guidelines work
rubrics_metrics.description: The agent notes 'sometimes I surprise myself with what I fall in love with, so please do query me even if your manuscript falls outside these guidelines!'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not be discouraged from querying if their project isn't an exact fit; exceptional or surprising work may still attract interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred/represented genres and favorite sub-genres (taste indicators)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of genres the agent handles: Fiction categories include Commercial, Crime, Family Saga, General, Historical, Horror, Humor, Literary, Mystery, Thriller, Women’s Fiction, Young Adult. Favorite sub-genres: Contemporary Romance, Historical Fantasy, Literary Fiction, Speculative Fiction, Suspense, Upmarket Fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These lists serve as explicit signals of the agent's breadth of interest and where your project might align; the page also lists 'all time favorites' and exemplar titles to convey taste.
